core_mechanisms_audited: Stale claim removal & level-triggered reaper convergence
Git push fence vs local commit durability (BestEffortPush)
GitHub comment truncation (>100 comments pagination failure)
Zombie fencing defeat & divergent local execution loops

heartbeat_and_self_fencing.design_model: DynamoDB Lock Client pattern with monotonic local clock observation. Heartbeat runs on a virtual thread executing in-place PATCH on the issue claim comment. The self-fencing threshold freezes the worker when consecutive heartbeat losses exceed lostDetection window, strictly before remote TTL expiration.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Premature live-holder reaping due to clock skew
attack_surfaces_audited.mechanism: StalenessMemory uses observer-local monotonic time (Duration.ofMinutes(15)). No synchronized wall clock is used. A freshly started instance cannot declare an existing claim stale before its own TTL has elapsed since first observation.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Transient network outage causing false claim loss
attack_surfaces_audited.mechanism: GithubHeartbeat distinguishes HTTP 404 (ClaimGone - definitive theft/reaping) from HTTP 5xx/IOException (TransportFailure). Only consecutive failures exceeding lostDetection freeze the worker.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Comment count exceeding 100 blinding heartbeat resolveClaim
attack_surfaces_audited.details: GithubHeartbeat.resolveClaim executes GET /issues/{num}/comments?per_page=100 without pagination. If the issue has >100 comments and the active claim was posted at index >= 101, resolveClaim returns Optional.empty(), causing GithubHeartbeat to return BeatResult.Lost(ClaimGone). A healthy live worker immediately self-fences due to pagination truncation.

stale_claim_removal_and_reaper.design_model: Level-triggered sweeper that inspects the union of listOpen and listReady(100). Evicts stale claims via atomic version-guarded delete (RemoveStaleClaimResult.Removed vs Mismatch).

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Reaper race against live heartbeat update (ABA problem)
attack_surfaces_audited.mechanism: GithubStaleClaimRemoval performs reReadThread before deleting comment. If comment updated_at or id changes, removal returns Mismatch and aborts deletion.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Double-holder race on stale claim reclaim
attack_surfaces_audited.mechanism: Once Reaper deletes comment and strips working label, task enters Ready. Next claimant must successfully post claim comment and verify it is the earliest winner in GithubClaimWindow.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Comment count exceeding 100 blinding reaper reReadThread
attack_surfaces_audited.details: GithubStaleClaimRemoval.reReadThread queries /comments?per_page=100. If newer activity pushed the claim or boundary beyond comment 100, the reaper operates on obsolete page 1 data.

claim_epoch_monotonicity.design_model: Opaque 64-bit integer derived from tracker comment ID. Stamped into Git commit trailers and tracker state markers as writer provenance.

findings.fence_role: Provenance stamp ONLY. ClaimEpoch is NEVER evaluated as a read-side admission filter or gate. It names the tenure that authored a commit.
findings.invariance: Because readers never reject older epochs upon checkout or resume, ClaimEpoch alone does not fence writers. Fencing is delegated entirely to Git push rejection and tracker round-boundary checks.

git_push_fence_vs_local_durability.design_model: ADR 0002 claims non-fast-forward push rejection serves as a hard fence against zombie workers. In reality, GitAttemptPersistence treats local git commit as the durability boundary, and BestEffortPush deliberately catches non-fast-forward push rejections and swallows them with a warning.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Local execution loop continues after remote push rejection
attack_surfaces_audited.details: BestEffortPush.pushBestEffort catches GitCommandResult when push fails (exit code != 0). It calls PushOutcome.describe and logs WARN OperatorEvent.PUSH_FAILED. It NEVER throws an exception. Therefore, GitAttemptPersistence.persist succeeds! The local worker believes round persistence succeeded and proceeds to RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Zombie fence verification in ZombieFenceSpec is dependent on tracker stub
attack_surfaces_audited.details: ZombieFenceSpec asserts that a zombie halts on revocation. However, inspection of ZombieFenceSpec demonstrates that the Git push rejection did not halt the execution; rather, the stubbed Tracker.fetchTask explicitly returned Working(NEW_HOLDER), triggering RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence. Revocation check halts ONLY if the tracker reports revocation.

truncation_defeat_of_revocation_fence.design_model: When a worker finishes a round, RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence calls tracker.fetchTask(ref). If the state is Working(holder) and holder == ourInstanceId, execution continues.

attack_surfaces_audited.attack: Full fence bypass via comment truncation (>100 comments)
attack_surfaces_audited.details: When an issue exceeds 100 comments, GithubTaskFetcher.fetchTask fetches only comments 1..100. If instance A was reaped and instance B claimed the task at comment #102: when zombie instance A calls fetchTask, it receives page 1 (comments 1..100) where instance A's claim is the latest visible claim. fetchTask returns Working('instance-A')! RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence checks holder.equals(instanceId.value()) which evaluates to TRUE! Consequently: (1) BestEffortPush swallowed the git non-fast-forward rejection, and (2) RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence passed because fetchTask returned stale holder A. Zombie instance A continues executing subsequent rounds locally, producing diverging local commits.

shapes.description: Ready label present, no active claim footprint. Available for claim.
Working label present, live claim comment with active heartbeat.
Parked label present, terminal or quarantined state (e.g. INFRA failure, abort threshold).
Finished label present, pipeline completed successfully.
Task explicitly released back to pool with returned state marker.
Claim revoked by operator or supervisory controller.
Working label applied, but claim comment write not yet observed or index lagging.
Claim released after failed resource resolution (e.g. git base unreachable); working label remains temporarily.
Labels and comment markers temporarily inconsistent due to asynchronous GitHub search/eventual consistency.
Issue labels or comments outside Gnomish namespace or unrecognized format.

kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.name: Tracker claim to task-creation commit
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.boundary: After tracker claim comment posted, before git STARTED commit
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.convergence: Reaper observes unchanged claim for TTL duration, deletes claim comment, resets label to Ready/no-branch.

kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.name: Failed base refresh release
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.boundary: After tracker claim, git origin unreachable during base resolution
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.convergence: FailedBaseRefreshRelease releases claim comment. Reaper detects working label with absent claim, resets label to Ready.

kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.name: Post-commit to push round
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.boundary: Local git commit created, before BestEffortPush completes
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.convergence: If holder lives, next round or retry pushes commit. If holder dies, reaper restores Ready; next claimant resumes from branch if pushed, or restarts round.

kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.name: Post-persist revocation check
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.boundary: After BestEffortPush returns, during tracker.fetchTask check
kill_windows_and_recovery_matrix.vulnerability_note: Defeated if issue has >100 comments: fetchTask returns stale holder, worker fails to self-fence.

remediation_recommendations.recommendation: Implement paginated comment fetching or fetch issue comments in reverse chronological order (direction=desc if supported, or follow Link headers) so the newest comments/claim markers are never truncated.

Do not treat non-fast-forward push failure as a non-fatal best-effort condition. If a push is rejected with non-fast-forward, throw a PushRejectedException immediately to halt local round progression, rather than relying exclusively on tracker checks.
Ensure IndexRepair scans all pages of comments before deciding latestBoundary is null, preventing destructive rollback of ABORT/FINISH boundaries.
